method.name: Map
method.brief: Map a page into an address space or update the mapping attributes.
method.description: Takes a VSpace capability as an argument and installs a reference to the given in the lowest-level unmapped paging structure corresponding to the given address, or updates the mapping attributes if the page is already mapped at this address. The page must not already be mapped through this capability in a different VSpace or at a different address; the page may be mapped in multiple VSpaces by copying the capability. Overmapping is allowed: if a different page of the same size is already mapped at this address, this mapping is replaced. The capability of the replaced page is not updated.

method.name: DeriveSubframe
method.brief: Derive 4 KiB aliases of a RAM-backed 2 MiB frame.
method.description: Derives count consecutive aliases, starting at offset, into consecutive slots of a destination CNode. The destination CNode, window and empty-slot checks are those of Untyped_Retype; nothing is derived unless every check passes. Offset must be 4 KiB aligned, and offset + count * 4 KiB must not exceed 2 MiB. Rights are intersected with the source's rights. Memory is neither allocated nor cleared. The results are unmapped and remain in the source Untyped's derivation tree, so revoking that Untyped deletes both sizes of aliases before memory reuse. Deleting the source leaves its aliases alive. Derived aliases and ordinary copies retain non-revocable frame-copy semantics: an alias does not gain authority to revoke other aliases.

param.name: root
param.description: CPtr to the CNode at the root of the destination CSpace.

param.name: node_index
param.description: CPtr to the destination CNode, resolved relative to the root parameter.

param.name: node_depth
param.description: Number of bits of node_index to translate; zero uses the root CNode itself.

param.name: node_offset
param.description: Slot of the destination CNode for the first alias.

param.name: offset
param.description: Byte offset in the large frame of the first alias.

param.name: count
param.description: Number of aliases to derive.

param.name: rights
param.description: Maximum derived rights.

method.name: TestAndClearAccessed
method.brief: Test and clear the accessed bit of a mapped 4 KiB or 2 MiB frame.
method.description: The mapping is located using the capability's ASID and address, and must still refer to the same frame. Clearing is atomic and does not invalidate the TLB: a cached translation can delay the observation of a later access. Permissions and dirty state are unchanged. Other sizes and non-native mappings are unsupported.

param.name: accessed
param.description: One if the accessed bit was set, otherwise zero.

error.name: seL4_IllegalOperation
error.description: The frame is not a mapped native 4 KiB or 2 MiB page.

error.name: seL4_InvalidCapability
error.description: The capability's mapping is stale.

method.name: IssueSGISignal
method.brief: Create a software generated interrupt (SGI) signal capability.
method.description:
Create an SGISignal capability and place it in the specific target CSpace slot. The capability can be used to raise an SGI with a specific ID on a specific target core. Currently this feature is supported on GICv2 and GICv3 hardware. Only available on non-SMP configurations.
The resulting capability can be invoked like a notification capability that supports only signal/send. SGIs can be received by IRQ notification objects on the target core like other IRQs. See also .
Note that the kernel only checks architectural limits for SGI IRQ id and target. It does not know whether the corresponding target core exists. Depending on hardware implementation, signalling a non-existent target may create an unrecoverable SError. This means it is the responsibility of the developer to not issue capabilities for targets that do not exist.

param.name: irq
param.description: The SGI INTID (0-15) that can be signalled.

param.name: target
param.description: The node ID that will be targeted. 0-7 for GICv2 and the affinity value for GICv3 (concatenation of Aff3+Aff2+Aff1+Aff0 from MPIDR). Targets within that range that are not supported by thde hardware will be not be rejected. For example, on a GICv2 board with 4 CPUs, the capability for target 5 can be created. The result of later signalling this target depends on the hardware implementation.

param.name: root
param.description: CPtr to the CNode that forms the root of the destination CSpace. Must be at a depth equivalent to the wordsize.

param.name: index
param.description: CPtr to the destination slot. Resolved from the root of the destination CSpace.

param.name: depth
param.description: Number of bits of dest_index to resolve to find the destination slot.
